  contract for up to two additional one-year terms in the annual
  amount of $581 ,350 (which includes a contingency of $52,850),

  Charles Peretz, Public Works Administrator with Parks and

D  Natural Resources, provided a PowerPoint presentation on the
  item; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember McAustin expressed concerns with the poor
  condition of camphor trees in her neighborhood. She requested
  additional information on the 25 percent pruning requirement; and
  the complaint process for contractors, including staff follow up;
  and inquired if staff reviews complaint history prior to awarding a
  contract to a vendor. She spoke on the importance that the City
  contractors interact with the residents in a professional and
  respectful manner, as representatives of the City.

  City Manager Mermell stated that staff divided the tree pruning
  contracts at the direction of the City Council in order to provide an
  opportunity for smaller and local businesses to submit proposals.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with the identical
  vendors bidding on similar tree pruning contracts; and spoke in
  favor of combining the pruning tree contracts, which would save
  City funds, and suggested imposing, as much as legally
  permissible, a local vendor element to the contract.
